title: Loop Engineering from First Principles — Kyle Mistele, HumanLayer
talk_summary: Kyle Mistele argues that blind 'Ralph' loops produce unreadable 40k-line PRs and are too expensive, and instead proposes agentic control loops (set point, sensor, controller, actuator) that make small incremental changes with feedback. He walks through a real internal loop migrating RPC procedures to Effect, including a disturbance dampener, a version-controlled feedback file for human re-steering, and flow control that caps one open PR per loop.

takeaways.what_they_do: Each loop iteration deterministically senses violations (AST-grep), picks one smallest/lowest-risk item, and an actuator agent makes a single incremental change, then commits and opens a PR.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can write a workflow that runs a single iteration of the loop, sense, control, actuate, and creates a PR

takeaways.what_they_do: Before running, the workflow checks if any PR with its loop label is still open; if so it exits, so loops never stack duplicate/conflicting work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can just check and see if the last PR that we created or any PR with the loops label on it is open. And if so, we just shut down

takeaways.technique: Version-controlled feedback file for human re-steering
takeaways.what_they_do: A markdown feedback file in the repo is deterministically loaded into the actuator's context each run; a /iterate PR comment triggers the agent to fix code and update that file, so corrections persist and are revertable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: create a feedback file that's tracked in version control just as a markdown file ... deterministically load it into our actuator agent's context every time

takeaways.technique: Deterministic sensor + disturbance dampener on main
takeaways.what_they_do: Full scan of main sorted deterministically and tracked in VCS; every new PR is checked for newly added violations so agents/teammates can't undo the loop's progress.

takeaways.technique: Hand-written golden patterns before agent rollout
takeaways.what_they_do: Engineers write idiomatic example implementations by hand and feed them to the actuator as patterns to replicate, instead of relying on docs or model priors.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we like to build out what we call golden patterns by hand before setting the agent loose ... because they're just pattern replicators

takeaways.technique: Split multi-item work into separate context windows
takeaways.what_they_do: When speeding up, the controller picks N items but runs each in its own implementation phase/context window rather than one giant run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: do each of those in a separate implementation phase, which will be both cheaper and more reliable since each migration gets its own context window
